records.definition: 整体中的一部分；本文指开始进行有兴趣、有条理的学习的大学生，尽管他们在大学生中所占比例很小。
records.otherSenses:
1) 比例关系（不可数）：两者在数量、大小等方面的关系
2) 均衡、匀称（不可数；可数时通常用复数）：各部分大小或重要性之间恰当的关系
3) proportions（复数）：大小、规模；尺寸和形状
4) 数学（不可数）：等比关系，如 4:8 = 6:12
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a small/large proportion of ... ……中的一小部分／很大一部分
a significant proportion of ... ……中相当大的一部分
the proportion of A to B A 与 B 的比例
in proportion to ... 与……成比例；与……相称
out of (all) proportion to ... 与……极不相称；程度远超应有水平
keep sth in proportion 客观看待某事，分清轻重

Contrast:
proportion：整体中某部分所占的份额，不要求写成数字
share：某人或某组在整体中的份额，也可指分得的一份
percentage：以百分数明确表示份额；说 20% 时可用 percentage

Usage Note:
a proportion of + 复数名词作主语时，谓语常用复数；the proportion of + 复数名词通常强调整体占比，谓语多用单数。原句 a proportion, however small, of college students do get ... 中，however small 是插入补充说明，do 强调“确实”。
records.examples: proportion: You shall remain liable for the fees although we may, at our discretion, refund you a proportion of the fees where we have been able to reallocate your place. [https://www.theguardian.com/guardian-masterclasses/2014/jun/04/terms-and-conditions]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· proportion
records.definitionEn: A part or share of a whole; here, the small share of college students who begin interested, methodical study.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) [uncountable] The relative size or amount of one thing compared with another.
2) [uncountable; countable usually plural] A balanced relationship between parts in size or importance.
3) proportions [plural]: the size and shape of something.
4) Mathematics [uncountable]: an equal relationship between two pairs of numbers.

records.definition: 细致、有条理的；本文修饰 study，指按清楚的思路和步骤进行的学习。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a methodical approach/study 有条理的方法／研究
a methodical search 有条理的搜查
be methodical in one’s work 工作有条不紊

Contrast:
methodical：有条理地逐步做事，强调细致和顺序
systematic：遵循一套完整的体系或计划，强调方法的一贯性
organized：安排得井然有序，未必强调每一步的逻辑

Usage Note:
methodical 可修饰人或做事方式：be methodical in one’s work；methodical study 指按步骤、有条理的学习。名词 method 是“方法”，methodology 多指一套研究方法或方法论。
records.examples: methodical: The east German politician, who has a degree in physics, is methodical, going through all options before making a decision. [https://www.economist.com/node/4401678?ah=0bca374e65f2354d553956ea65f756e0&zid=295]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· methodical
records.definitionEn: Done in a careful and logical way; here, it describes the students’ careful, orderly study.

records.definition: 论题、主张；本文指作者以事实和个人经历支持的大学教育观点。
records.otherSenses: 1) 学位论文：学生基于个人研究、为取得大学学位而完成的长篇文章
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
prove/support a thesis 证明／支持一个论点（本文义）
advance/argue/develop the thesis that ... 提出／论证／展开……这一论题
submit a thesis on sth 提交关于某主题的学位论文（另一义）

Contrast:
thesis：文章或论证要支持的中心主张
central claim：核心论点，语气比 thesis 普通
contention：有争议、需要论证的主张，较正式

Usage Note:
本文 prove my thesis 中的 thesis 是“论点”，不是“学位论文”。表达论点可用 the thesis that ...；指学位论文可说 a thesis on sth。复数为 theses /ˈθiːsiːz/。
records.examples: thesis: Mr Ponta has also been accused of plagiarising his PhD thesis and lying in his CV. [https://www.economist.com/europe/2012/12/15/clear-victory-uncertain-future]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· thesis
records.definitionEn: A statement or opinion argued logically and supported with evidence; here, the author’s claim about university education.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) A long piece of writing based on a student’s own research and completed as part of a university degree.

records.definition: 用事例说明、阐明；本文指作者的个人经历说明了他的论点。
records.otherSenses:
1) 给书籍等加插图或图表
2) 表明某事属实或某种情况确实存在
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
illustrate a point 说明一个观点
illustrate sth with examples/pictures 用例子／图片说明某事
illustrate how/what ... 举例说明如何／什么……
illustrate that ... 表明……

Contrast:
illustrate：用事例或图像使观点更清楚
exemplify：以某人或某事充当观点的实例
demonstrate：以事实或证据说明观点成立，论证力度通常更强

Usage Note:
illustrate 是及物动词：illustrate sth；也可说 illustrate sth with sth，或接 how/what/that 从句。本文 illustrates it 的 it 回指 thesis，指“说明论点”，不是“给书配插图”。
records.examples: illustrate: He uses both authors to illustrate how, by the early 19th century, it was logical to disdain work in favour of marrying into wealth.  [https://www.theguardian.com/books/2014/apr/28/thomas-piketty-capital-surprise-bestseller]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· illustrate
records.definitionEn: To make a point clearer by using an example; here, the author’s experience illustrates his thesis.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) To add pictures, photographs or diagrams to a book or similar work.
2) To show that something is true or that a situation exists.

records.definition: 设法绕过或克服阻碍；本文指找到办法，不让教师、其他学生和僵化的大学制度妨碍自己的学习。
records.otherSenses:
1) 四处走动；从一处到另一处
2) （非正式）到许多不同的地方旅行
3) （消息等）传播开来
4) 通过讨好等方式说服某人同意或照自己的意思做
5) get around to sth/doing：终于抽出时间或找到机会做某事；注意多了介词 to，与绕过障碍的 get around sth 不同。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
get around/get round a problem 设法解决或绕过难题
get around/get round a clause 设法绕过条款
get around with the help of a stick 拄着手杖四处走动
news gets around 消息传开

Contrast:
get around：设法绕过阻碍或限制
circumvent：有意绕开障碍、规则或限制，较正式
get past：越过难关或阻碍，强调最终得以继续

Usage Note:
get around an obstacle 表“绕过障碍”；英式英语也常说 get round。get around somebody 则可能表示设法说服某人，须看宾语和上下文。
records.examples: get around: In order to get around the limitation rule, he sent his illiterate manservant off to the British Museum to find a copy of the Weekly Dispatch article published some 17 years previously. [https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/libertycentral/2009/sep/24/multiple-publication-libel-tourists]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· get around
records.definitionEn: To find a way to deal successfully with an obstacle; here, to get past the faculty, other students and the college system.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) To move from place to place.
2) (Informal) To travel to many different places.
3) For news or information to spread.
4) To persuade somebody to agree or do what you want, often by being nice to them.
5) get around to something: finally find time or an opportunity to do it

records.definition: （北美英语）大学或学院的全体教师；本文指作者设法绕过其影响的大学教师群体。
records.otherSenses:
1) （可数）高等院校的学部、学院或相关院系组成的部门
2) （通常复数）与生俱来的感官或思维能力
3) （正式；单数）做某事的特定才能
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
faculty members 大学教师；某院系教师
a faculty meeting 教师会议
the Faculty of Law 法学院
mental faculties 心智能力
a faculty for doing sth 做某事的才能

Contrast:
faculty：北美英语中大学的教师群体
teaching staff：授课教师群体，通常不包括行政员工
academic staff：大学的学术人员，也可能包括以研究为主的人员

Usage Note:
北美英语用 the faculty 指大学教师群体；英式英语 faculty 常指大学里的学院或学部。faculty 表“天生官能”时常用复数 faculties，a faculty for sth 表特定才能。
records.examples: faculty: First, student protesters are backed by faculty and parents. [https://www.economist.com/britain/2003/03/06/dream-on]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· faculty
records.definitionEn: The teachers of a college or university (North American English); here, the teachers the author tries to work around.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) [countable] A university department or group of related departments.
2) [countable, usually plural] Natural physical or mental abilities.
3) [singular, formal] A particular ability for doing something.

records.definition: 使思想定型、把人的思考限制在既定框架内。它是作者在本文语境中构成的批评性表达。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
the system of mind-fixing 使思想定型的制度（本文自造表达；没有可直接套用的现代固定搭配）
fixed ways of thinking 固定的思维方式（相关表达）
independent thinking 独立思考（语义对照）

Usage Note:
mind-fixing 由 mind + fixing 组成；fix 在这里表示“使固定”，整个复合词指把思想限制在既定框架内。它是作者的批评性造词，改写时可用固定思维方式等更自然的表达。
records.examples:
John Stuart Mill observes: "Those only are happy who have their minds fixed on some object other than their own happiness … Aiming thus at something else, they find happiness along the way".
[https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/belief/2011/aug/08/christianity-us-collapsing-america]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — mind（mind-fixing 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: A context-specific compound meaning the process of fixing people's minds within accepted patterns and limiting independent thought.

records.definition: 学位；本文两处 degree 都指完成大学课程后取得的学位。
records.otherSenses:
1) 程度；水平（可数或不可数）
2) 温度的度数（可数）
3) 角的度数（可数）
4) （英式英语）大学学位课程（可数）
5) 严重程度的级别（可数），如一级谋杀、三度烧伤
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
get/earn a degree 获得学位
a degree in sth 某学科的学位
a bachelor’s/master’s/doctoral degree 学士／硕士／博士学位
a high degree of sth 很大程度的……
to a certain degree 在一定程度上

Contrast:
degree：完成大学课程后授予的学位
academic qualification：学术资格或学历，范围比 degree 广
diploma：完成课程获得的文凭，不能直接视为同等级的学位

Usage Note:
本文 his degree、a degree 都是可数的“学位”；a degree in history 表示历史学学位。表示“程度”可说 a degree of skill、to a certain degree。by degrees 表“逐渐地”；to the nth degree 表“到极端程度”。
records.examples: degree: He admitted that when the virus first struck "there was probably a lack of knowledge and there was a certain degree of arrogance", but he said he believed lessons were being learned. [https://app.ludwig.guru/s/degree]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· degree
records.definitionEn: A qualification gained after successfully completing a university or college course; both uses in the sentence refer to this academic qualification.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) [countable or uncountable] The amount or level of something.
2) [countable] A unit for measuring temperature.
3) [countable] A unit for measuring angles.
4) [countable, British English] A university or college course leading to a degree.
5) [countable] A level on a scale of seriousness.

records.definition: 有……价值；本文 not worth so much as 表示“价值不如……”，即学位不如学习能力与动力重要。
records.otherSenses:
1) 形容词：值某个金额或数量
2) 形容词：某种行动值得做，可接动名词
3) 形容词：某人拥有某个金额的财产
4) 名词（不可数）：值某个金额或够用一段时间的数量
5) 价值；作用；重要性，不限于货币金额。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
be worth + money 值多少钱
be worth a visit 值得参观
be worth doing sth 值得做某事
be worth it 值得付出
be worth somebody’s while 对某人有好处；值得某人花时间

Contrast:
worth：通常作表语，后接金额、名词或 -ing，表示有某种价值或值得做
valuable：可作定语或表语，强调有用或有价值
worthwhile：多修饰活动或努力，强调值得投入时间和精力

Usage Note:
worth 作形容词通常不放在名词前，后接名词、代词、数额或动名词；说 worth doing，不说 worth to do。本文 not worth so much as 在比较价值。for what it’s worth 是非正式口吻，表示“这只是我的看法，不一定有帮助”；worth its weight in gold 表“非常有用”。
records.examples: worth: Teddy Roosevelt once observed that life's greatest gift is the opportunity to work hard at work worth doing. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2012/nov/09/barack-obama-debt-deal-live]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· worth
records.definitionEn: Having a particular value; here, a degree is less valuable than the capacity and drive to learn.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Adjective: having a stated monetary or measurable value.
2) Adjective: useful or pleasant enough to recommend an action.
3) Adjective: owning money and possessions of a stated value.
4) Noun [uncountable]: an amount with a stated value or lasting a stated time.
5) the usefulness, importance or value of a person or thing

records.definition: 此处表示：学位的价值不如学习能力和学习动力。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
A is worth as much as B：A 和 B 同样有价值
A is not worth so/as much as B：A 的价值不及 B（本文）
did not / never so much as + 动词原形：甚至连……都没做
without so much as + -ing / 名词：连……都没有
not so much A as B：与其说 A，不如说 B

Contrast:
not worth so much as：价值不及；本文用法
not worth as much as：同义的现代比较表达
less valuable than：直接说价值较低，句法结构不同

Usage Note:
原句是 a degree is not [worth so much as the capacity and the drive to learn]。worth 使句子在比较价值，整句可改写成 a degree is not worth as much as the capacity and the drive to learn；这就是判断本文用法的关键。
“甚至连……”通常跟一个最低限度的动作或东西：He did not so much as smile；He did not say so much as a word。without 是介词，后接 -ing 或名词：without so much as saying goodbye。
“与其说 A，不如说 B”要求 A、B 是同一事物的两种平行描述。原句中的 worth 与 the capacity and the drive to learn 不构成这样的 A、B 对照。
records.examples: so/as much as: Understand it's never worth as much as you think it is, and from a personal perspective, it's not worth it at all. [https://www.theguardian.com/media/2002/oct/01/comment]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — much（so/as much as 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: Here, a degree is less valuable than the capacity and drive to learn.

records.definition: 理解或做某事的能力；本文 the capacity to learn 指学习的能力。
records.otherSenses:
1) 容器或场所的容量（不可数；可数时通常单数）
2) 履行职责时的身份或角色（可数，通常单数）
3) 工厂、机器等的产能（单数或不可数）
4) 尤指发动机的容积或功率（可数或不可数）
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
the capacity to do sth 做某事的能力（本文用法）
a capacity for sth/doing sth 对某事／做某事的能力
seating/storage capacity 容纳人数／存储容量
in one’s capacity as ... 以……的身份
at full capacity 满负荷运转

Contrast:
capacity：潜在的能力或容纳能力；本文是学习能力
ability：最普通的“能做某事的能力”
capability：具备完成特定任务的本领，也常用于机器或机构

Usage Note:
本文 capacity to learn 是“学习能力”；也可说 capacity for learning。capacity 作“能力”时可数或不可数，通常用单数；作“职位／身份”常见 in one’s capacity as ...，作“生产能力”常见 at full capacity，作“场所容量”可说 filled to capacity。复数为 capacities。
records.examples: capacity: For someone who woke up at 1.30am in Germany, her capacity for exuberant chatter is remarkable.[https://www.theguardian.com/music/2011/oct/20/kelly-clarkson-stronger-american-idol]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· capacity
records.definitionEn: The ability to understand or do something; here, the capacity to learn means the ability to learn.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) [uncountable; countable usually singular] The amount that a container or space can hold.
2) [countable, usually singular] An official position or function in which someone acts.
3) [singular or uncountable] The amount that a factory or machine can produce.
4) [countable or uncountable] The size or power of a piece of equipment, especially an engine.

records.definition: 冲劲、干劲；本文 the drive to learn 指促使人持续学习的强烈内在动力。
records.otherSenses:
1) 名词：驾车行程；兜风
2) 名词：为某一目标开展的有组织活动
3) 名词：人的本能欲望或需求（如性欲）
4) 名词：计算机存储驱动器
5) 名词：通往住宅的私人车道
6) 动词：驾驶车辆；驾车送某人
7) 动词：迫使或驱使某人做某事
8) 动词：推动某事发展或取得进展
9) 动词：为机器提供动力；驱动设备
10) 把钉子等打入；驱赶人或动物朝某方向移动。
11) （体育）猛击、抽击或有力的一投；用力击球或投球。
12) （雨、风等）猛落；猛烈吹袭。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
the drive to learn/succeed 学习／成功的动力（本文用法）
have tremendous drive 干劲十足
a recruitment drive 招聘活动
drive sb to do sth 迫使／驱使某人做某事
be driven by sth 受……推动
drive growth/investment 推动增长／投资

Contrast:
drive：促使人不断行动的内在干劲
motivation：促使行动的动机或积极性，范围较广
determination：决心与坚持，突出不轻易放弃

Usage Note:
本文 drive 是不可数名词，the drive to learn 表学习的内在动力。表示驾车行程、招聘活动、电脑驱动器或私人车道时通常可数；动词可用 drive sb to do sth。
records.examples: drive: Back then they had vision, drive and the desire to make the world of education a better place. [https://www.theguardian.com/teacher-network/2015/mar/07/secret-teacher-school-managers]
records.dictionaryLabel: 牛津高阶英汉双解词典（第10版）· drive
records.definitionEn: Strong energy and determination to achieve something; here, the drive to learn is a strong inner urge to keep learning.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Noun: a journey in a car or other vehicle.
2) Noun: an organized effort to achieve a goal.
3) Noun: a strong instinctive need, such as sex drive.
4) Noun: a computer device for storing data.
5) Noun: a private road leading from a street to a house.
6) Verb: to operate a vehicle or take someone somewhere in it.
7) Verb: to force or motivate someone to act.
8) Verb: to influence something and make it progress.
9) Verb: to provide power for a machine or operate a device.
10) force an object into a surface or move animals or people in a particular direction
11) a forceful stroke or throw; to hit or throw a ball with force
12) fall or blow with strong force, especially of rain or wind

records.definition: 偶然想到（主意或方法）；本文指作者偶然想出了自己的学习方法。
records.otherSenses: 1) hit on somebody（北美俚语）：与某人搭讪、调情，表示性方面的兴趣
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
hit on/upon an idea 偶然想到一个主意
hit on the right solution 突然想到合适的办法
hit on a title 灵机一动想到标题

Contrast:
hit on/upon：突然或偶然想到主意或办法
think of：想到，不强调是否偶然
come up with：想出可用的主意或解决办法

Usage Note:
表示“想到主意”常说 hit on/upon an idea。原文 My method was hit on by accident 是被动写法；现代日常表达通常说 I hit on a method by accident。hit on somebody 在北美俚语中另有搭讪义。
records.examples: hit on: She hit on a scheme.[https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/1951/08/25/musicale]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · hit on (user-provided Eudic entry)
records.definitionEn: To think of an idea or method suddenly or by chance; here, the author found his study method accidentally.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) hit on somebody (North American English, slang): to approach someone in a sexually interested way.

records.definition: 偶然地、无意中；本文表示作者的方法并非事先设计出来的。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
meet somebody by accident 偶然遇到某人
happen by accident 偶然发生
purely by accident 完全出于偶然
by accident or design 偶然还是有意

Contrast:
by accident：偶然地、无意中，强调并非有意安排
by chance：碰巧发生，强调机会或偶然性
accidentally：副词，通常可替换 by accident

Usage Note:
by accident 是副词短语，修饰动作；原文 was hit on by accident 表示“偶然想到”。不要把 accident 的各种名词义直接套用到短语 by accident 上。
records.examples: by accident: It could not have happened by accident. [https://www.newyorker.com/news/hendrik-hertzberg/heritage-diagnosed-severe-demintia].
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · by accident (user-provided Eudic entry)
records.definitionEn: By chance, without planning or intending it; here, the author did not deliberately devise his method.

records.definition: 本能的直觉；本文指作者选择学习方式时受到某种直觉的引导。
records.otherSenses: 1) 与生俱来的行为倾向或本能，不靠后天学习获得
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
by instinct / on instinct 凭本能；凭直觉
trust/follow one's instincts 相信／遵循直觉
one's first instinct is to do sth 第一反应是做某事
an instinct for business 对经商有天生的感觉／才能

Contrast:
instinct：未经仔细推理而产生的本能感觉或倾向
intuition：对某事的直觉理解或判断
gut feeling：非正式说法，强调说不清缘由的直觉

Usage Note:
instinct 可作不可数或可数名词；本文 some instinct 用不可数形式。说 instinct for sth 可表示对某事的天赋，instinct about sb/sth 可表示对人或事的直觉判断。
records.examples: instinct: My instinct when I look at this photo is to grab that girl and protect her, her social awkwardness, in the same way I want to protect my little girl who is six and identical to me. [https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2023/mar/04/jessie-cave-looks-back]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · instinct (user-provided Eudic entry)
records.definitionEn: An intuitive feeling rather than a planned decision; here, some instinct helped guide the author's study choices.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) An inborn tendency to act in a particular way without learning or training.

records.definition: 专攻某一领域；本文指作者选定自己感兴趣的学科，集中深入学习。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
specialize in history/law 专攻历史／法律
specialize in doing sth 专门从事某事
a shop specializing in sth 专营某类商品的商店

Contrast:
specialize in：长期专攻某一领域并形成专长
major in：在大学正式主修某学科，尤见于美式英语
focus on：把精力集中在某事，可只是暂时的

Usage Note:
specialize 可单独作不及物动词，如原文 I specialized；说明具体领域时用 specialize in sth，不用 specialize on。英式拼写也作 specialise。
records.examples: specialize: The priests specialize in arrogance, the nuns in humility.As for the nuns themselves, some have declined to comment, because they have to be obedient. [https://www.economist.com/democracy-in-america/2012/04/26/nuns-gone-wild]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · specialize (user-provided Eudic entry)
records.definitionEn: To focus one's study on a particular field; here, the author chose subjects that interested him and studied them deeply.

records.definition: 正式规定、指定；本文 prescribed courses 指学校规定必须修读的课程。
records.otherSenses: 1) 医学用法：给病人开具药物或规定治疗方法
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
prescribed courses/reading 规定须修的课程／指定阅读材料
prescribe which books should be studied 指定应学习哪些书
prescribe medicine for somebody 给某人开药

Contrast:
prescribe：由有权者明确规定具体做法
stipulate：在规则、合同或要求中清楚写明条件
require：要求必须做到，未必具体指定做法

Usage Note:
原文 With several courses prescribed 中，prescribed 是过去分词，说明几门课程已被学校规定。这里是“规定课程”，不是“开药”。prescribe something / prescribe that ... 都可用于规定义。
records.examples: prescribe: For example, the clinician could decide to see the patient more frequently or prescribe a different medication. [https://www.economist.com/lexingtons-notebook/2013/03/13/why-the-nra-keeps-talking-about-mental-illness-rather-than-guns]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · prescribe (user-provided Eudic entry)
records.definitionEn: To specify officially what must be done; here, the school required the student to take certain courses.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) In medicine, to tell a patient to use a particular medicine or treatment, or to write a prescription for it.

records.definition: 专注于……；本文指作者集中学习最感兴趣的一两门课程。
records.otherSenses:
1) concentrate：集中；聚集人、力量或物品。
2) concentrate：浓缩；提高浓度。
3) concentrate：浓缩物；浓缩液。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
concentrate on sth 专注于某事
concentrate on doing sth 专心做某事
concentrate one's efforts/energies on sth 把精力集中在某事上

Contrast:
concentrate on：把注意力或精力集中在某事上
focus on：把关注点放在某事上，含义较广
devote attention to：将注意力投入某事，后接名词或 -ing

Usage Note:
on 是介词，后接名词或 -ing：concentrate on reading，不说 concentrate on to read。原文 the one or two 指前面的 courses，that interested me most 修饰这些课程。
records.examples: For the first time I did not need a Saturday job. I could concentrate on my studies and write for the Newcastle University student newspaper. [https://www.theguardian.com/education/2022/apr/17/poorer-students-will-bear-the-brunt-of-costly-loans]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · concentrate (user-provided Eudic entry)
records.definitionEn: To give focused attention to something; here, the author focused on the one or two courses that interested him most.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) concentrate: gather or bring people or things together in one place
2) concentrate: make a liquid or substance stronger by removing water or unwanted material
3) concentrate: a substance whose water or other less useful parts have been removed

records.definition: 集中而深入地；本文指作者在喜爱的学科上投入大量精力。
records.otherSenses: 1) 以高投入、高产出的集约方式，尤用于农业；不能简单等同于 intensely（强烈地）。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
work/study intensively 高强度地工作／学习
investigate sth intensively 深入调查某事
intensive training/course 强化训练／密集课程（形容词）

Contrast:
intensively：高强度、密集地投入学习或工作
intently：十分专注地看或听，重点在注意力
thoroughly：全面、彻底地做完，重点在完整程度

Usage Note:
intensively 是副词，修饰 worked；intensive 是形容词，常修饰 training、course 或 investigation。intense 多形容感受、竞争等“强烈”，intensive 强调活动密集、投入大。
records.examples: intensively: Both sides have been intensively preparing for what each says will be a "decisive" second round.Such a war would bear little resemblance to the previous clashes between Israel and its neighbours. [https://www.economist.com/leaders/2010/12/29/please-not-again]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · intensive (user-provided adjective entry; adverb interpreted in context)
records.definitionEn: With concentrated effort; here, the author worked hard and deeply on his favorite subjects.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) with high inputs and high production in a small area, especially in farming

records.definition: （美式英语）大学三年级的；本文 junior year 指四年制大学的第三学年。
records.otherSenses:
1) 形容词：职位或级别较低的
2) 形容词：青少年组的，尤用于体育
3) 形容词（英式英语）：面向约 11 或 13 岁以下儿童的学校阶段

5) 名词（美式英语）：四年制高中或大学的三年级学生
6) 名词：比某人年轻若干岁的人，见 be somebody's junior

records.supplementation:

junior year 大学三年级这一学年（本文义）

records.examples: junior: To date, only one cabinet minister and a few junior officials have been arrested. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/may/20/malawi-election-2014-not-perfect-but-good-start]

records.otherSensesEn:
1) Adjective: lower in rank or position.

3) Adjective (British English): for children under about 11 or 13 at school.
4) Junior/Jr after a man's name: indicating he has the same name as his father.
5) Noun (North American English): a student in the third year of high school or college.
6) Noun, in be somebody's junior: a person younger than somebody else by a stated number of years.
7) a person with a lower rank in a job or organization; also a young member of a group

records.definition: 容易的事（非正式）；本文 several cinches in history 很可能指作者认为容易应付的几门历史课程或要求，课程义是结合上下文推断的。
records.otherSenses:
1) 名词（尤北美英语）：十拿九稳的事；必定成功的人
2) 动词：在腰间束紧；给马系上肚带
3) 动词（北美非正式）：确保某事发生或成功

records.supplementation:

a cinch 很容易的事；小菜一碟
be a cinch to do sth 做某事轻而易举
be a cinch to win 胜利几乎是板上钉钉的事（另一义）

Contrast:
a cinch：轻而易举的事，非正式
a piece of cake：非常容易的事，非正式，语气轻松
a breeze：做起来毫不费力的事，非正式

records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · cinch (user-provided noun and verb entries)
records.definitionEn: An easy task (informal); in context, several cinches in history probably means history courses or requirements the author found easy.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Noun (especially North American English): an event certain to happen, or a person certain to succeed.
2) Verb: to fasten something tightly around the waist or fasten a horse's girth.
3) Verb (North American English, informal): to make something certain.
4) a strap that passes under a horse to hold a saddle in place

records.definition: 忽视、未予重视；本文指作者过去没有认真学习历史。
records.otherSenses:
1) 动词：疏于照顾某人、健康或财物
2) neglect to do sth（正式）：疏忽、漏做本应做的事
3) 名词（不可数）：缺乏应有的照顾或重视
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
neglect one's studies/duties 忽视学业／职责
neglect a child / one's health 疏于照顾孩子／健康
neglect to mention sth 漏提某事

ignore：注意到了却有意不理会

原文 I had neglected it 中 it 指 history；过去完成时表示此前一直没有充分重视历史。neglect sth 后接名词；neglect to do sth 后接不定式，表示漏做本应做的事。名词 neglect 通常不可数。
records.examples: neglect: When a child dies of neglect or abuse, the local authority is accused of incompetence and negligence; if there is an outbreak of foot and mouth disease, claims about inadequate precautions are heard; former employees of companies which have collapsed during the recession demand to know why more has not been done to save their jobs. [https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2009/aug/21/obama-healthcare-britain-recession-government]

1) Verb: to fail to care properly for a person, health or property.

3) Noun [uncountable]: lack of necessary care or attention.

records.definition: 对某种做法强烈反感、抵触；本文指作者反感当时教授历史的方式。
records.otherSenses:

rebel at the way sth is done 对某事的做法感到强烈抵触（本文）

rebel against authority / one's parents 反抗权威／父母
rebel forces 叛军

object to：明确表示不赞同，不一定采取行动
balk at：因不愿接受而犹豫或拒绝，尤指提议或要求

1) rebel against somebody or something: fight against authority or refuse to obey it

positive knowledge 被视为确定的知识（本文）

records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · commit (user-provided verb entry)
records.definitionEn: To learn something so well that it can be recalled exactly; here, the author could not memorize facts he neither understood nor needed for his thinking.

records.definition: 在思考和理解层面；本文 intellectually need 指作者在思想探索上真正觉得需要。

intellectually challenging/stimulating 有智力挑战性／启发思考的

cognitively：从认知过程方面说，多见于学术语境

records.definitionEn: In a way connected with thinking and understanding; here, facts the author did not feel he needed for serious thought.

records.definition: 只有基本事实、缺少解释的；本文 bare record 指只罗列人名、日期和事件，却不说明相互联系的记录。

1) 指身体：裸露的，未被衣物遮盖的
2) 指树木或土地：光秃的、没有植被的
3) 指物体或表面：无遮盖、无保护的
4) 指房间或柜子：空的，缺少通常的物品
5) 用于名词前：仅够的；最低限度的
6) bare（动词）：揭开；暴露
7) bare（英式俚语副词）：非常

records.supplementation:

bare facts / the bare record 最基本的事实／仅有事实的记录（本文）
the bare minimum / bare essentials 最低限度／最基本的必需品
bare feet / bare hands 赤脚／徒手
lay sth bare 揭露某事（动词习语）

bare：只剩基本部分，没有额外装饰或解释
skeletal：只有骨架或简略内容，常说 a skeletal outline
stripped-down：删去不必要部分后的简化版本，较口语

Usage Note:
本文 bare 在名词 record 前，表示记录只剩基本事实。不要与同音的 bear（熊；承担）混淆；barely 是“几乎不／勉强”，不等于 bare。bare bones 指梗概；bare your soul 是动词短语，意为倾诉内心。

Word-formation note:
barely 常表示“几乎不；仅仅”，不是把 bare“裸露的”简单加上 -ly 后得到“赤裸地”的透明方式副词。
records.examples: bare: This bare record of Birks' distinguished career, however, gives no idea of the man. [https://www.theguardian.com/news/2004/jul/16/guardianobituaries.obituaries]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · bare (user-provided adjective, verb and adverb entries)
records.definitionEn: Basic and without explanatory detail; here, a bare record lists names, dates and events without showing their connections.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Of the body: uncovered by clothes.
2) Of trees or land: without leaves or vegetation.
3) Of an object or surface: without a covering or protection.
4) Of a room or cupboard: empty or lacking its usual contents.
5) Before a noun: only just enough; the minimum necessary.
6) bare (verb): to uncover or reveal something.
7) bare (British slang adverb): very.
8) bare: a large number or amount of something

records.definition: 彼此无关、缺乏有意义联系的。本文形容一连串孤立、互不关联的历史事件。
records.otherSenses:
1) （罕见/旧式）与当前问题无关；现代通常用 irrelevant
2) （罕见/旧式）与另一人或事物没有关系；现代通常用 unrelated
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
irrelative events 彼此缺乏联系的事件（本文旧式用法）
unrelated/unconnected events 互不相关的事件（现代转述）
be irrelevant to sth 与某个话题或判断无关（另一义）

Contrast:
irrelative：旧式、罕见；本文指事件彼此没有联系
unrelated：现代常用，指没有关联
unconnected：现代常用，突出没有联系或衔接

Usage Note:
irrelative 是罕见、旧式的形容词；本文修饰 events，强调事件之间缺乏联系。现代转述本文意思宜用 unrelated 或 unconnected，不能直接把它改成“与当前话题无关”的 irrelevant。
若要说某项信息对正在讨论的问题无关，现代英语可用 irrelevant to。
records.examples: irrelative: The trouble is that issues pertaining to north of the border are almost totally irrelevant in the 2011 Irish general election.  [https://www.theguardian.com/world/blog/2011/feb/10/fianna-fail-becomes-party-dare-not-speak-its-name]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — irrelevant（irrelative 无独立词条；链接现代常用近义词）
records.definitionEn: Rare and old-fashioned: not related to one another or lacking a meaningful connection; here, a series of isolated historical events.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Rare/old-fashioned: not important to or connected with the matter being considered; modern English usually uses irrelevant
2) Rare/old-fashioned: having no relation to another person or thing; modern English usually uses unrelated

records.definition: 提供信息，使某事更容易理解；阐明。本文指历史能够帮助理解表面上并非历史的问题。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
throw light on/upon sth 阐明某事（本文使用 upon，并把 light 与 throw upon 拆开）
throw light on a problem/the cause 阐明问题／原因
shed light on sth 提供有助于理解某事的信息（现代常见近义搭配）

Contrast:
throw light on/upon：提供线索，使问题更清楚
shed light on：与之意思接近，现代书面语常用
illuminate：阐明较抽象的问题，语气更书面

Usage Note:
throw/cast/shed light on/upon sth 表“阐明某事”。原句 history had light to throw upon ... 把这一习语拆开：light 是 to throw 的逻辑宾语；unhistorical questions 在这里指历史学以外的问题。
records.examples: throw light upon: All human resources — art, religion, literature, philosophy, and the historical sciences — all have joined in the attempt to throw light upon this darkness. [https://www.newyorker.com/?p=2895969]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries — light（throw/shed light on/upon 无独立词条）
records.definitionEn: To provide information that makes something easier to understand; here, to help explain matters that may not appear historical on the surface.

records.definition: 打算、计划做某事。本文 proposed ... to specialize in history 指作者决定在大三和大四专攻历史。
records.otherSenses:
1) 提出计划、想法或行动建议，供人考虑。
2) 在正式会议上提名某人或提出动议。
3) 向某人求婚。
4) propose a toast：提议为某人祝酒。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
propose to do sth 打算做某事
propose doing sth 提议或打算做某事（依语境）
propose that sb (should) do sth 提议某人做某事
propose a plan 提出计划

Contrast:
propose to do：打算亲自做某事，较正式
intend to do：有意做某事，突出意图
plan to do：已有做某事的计划，通常更具体

Usage Note:
本文 propose to specialize = “打算亲自专攻”；propose to do sth 常表示说话者自己的打算，语气较正式。
propose doing sth 可表示“提议做”或“打算做”，须看上下文；How do you propose getting home? 是“你打算怎么回家？”
propose that sb (should) do sth 表示提出建议；求婚用 propose to sb。
records.examples: propose: We will propose a 'double majority' rule – meaning that unless England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland each vote to leave the EU, as well as the UK as a whole, Britain would remain a member state. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2015/may/24/voting-age-eu-referendum-lowered-snp]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · propose (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: To intend or plan to do something; here, to plan to specialize in history during the junior and senior years.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) To suggest a plan, idea or action for others to consider.
2) To nominate someone or put a motion before a formal meeting.
3) To ask someone to marry you.
4) propose a toast: to invite people to raise their glasses to someone.

records.definition: 专心地、认真地。本文指作者聚精会神地听教授第一次介绍课程。
records.otherSenses: 1) 体贴、周到地照料他人所需。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
listen attentively 专心听
watch attentively 专注地看
read attentively 认真阅读

Contrast:
attentively：把注意力放在所听或所看的内容上
intently：聚精会神，强调专注程度
carefully：仔细或谨慎，重点也可能是避免出错

Usage Note:
listen 是不及物动词：listen attentively to the talk，不能省略 to。
attentive to sb/sth 指对人或事留心；attend a lecture 指出席，不等于一定专心听。
records.examples: attentively: We all listened attentively to this voice hoping it will say something to calm people. [https://www.independent.co.uk/voices/comment/i-wish-had-not-been-in-that-syrian-hospital-i-wish-i-had-not-seen-what-i-saw-after-the-duoma-air-attacks-10463877.html]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · attentively (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Carefully and with a great deal of interest; here, listening to the professor's first introduction with full concentration.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) To act helpfully and considerately so that people have what they need.

records.definition: 与国家宪法及其发展有关的。本文 American constitutional history 指美国宪政史。
records.otherSenses:
1) 符合宪法，或受到宪法限制。
2) 与人的体质或整体健康状况有关。
3) constitutional（旧式名词）：保健散步。
4) 天生的；性情或体质所固有的，不仅用于政治宪法。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
constitutional law 宪法
constitutional history 宪政史
constitutional rights 宪法权利
constitutional government 宪政政府

Usage Note:
constitutional 有“涉及宪法”与“合宪”两义：constitutional history 是宪法或宪政制度的发展史，不是“合宪的历史”。
a constitutional right 指宪法赋予或保障的权利；constitutionally protected 中用副词修饰 protected。
records.examples: constitutional: His lasting achievement was to persuade Margaret Thatcher to establish the Anglo Irish agreement in 1985 which gave Dublin some say over Northern Ireland affairs and was meant to bolster northern nationalist confidence in constitutional politics. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2011/may/19/garret-fitzgerald-tributes-statesman-achievement]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · constitutional (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Connected with a country's constitution and its development; here, American constitutional history.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Allowed or limited by a constitution.
2) Of a person's general health or physical makeup.
3) constitutional (noun, old-fashioned): a short walk taken for health.
4) existing as part of a person’s nature or physical make-up

records.definition: 供查阅或进一步研究的资料、书目。本文 some other references 指教授列出的补充参考资料。
records.otherSenses:
1) 在言语或文字中提及某人或某事。
2) 查阅资料以获得信息。
3) 帮助查找信息的编号、文字或符号。
4) 向某人征求意见或批准。
5) 求职推荐信，或提供推荐意见的人。
6) 书中注明信息出处的参考文献或引文。
7) reference（正式动词）：引用资料，或给文本附上参考文献。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
list/check references 列出／查阅参考资料（本文义）
a reference book 参考书
make reference to sth 提到某事（另一义）
a reference to sth 对某事的提及（另一义）

Contrast:
reference：可供查阅以获得信息的资料
source：资料或信息的来源，未必已列作参考书目
resource：可供学习或研究使用的材料，范围较广

Usage Note:
本文 other references 是教授建议进一步查阅的书籍或资料，不是“推荐人”。reference 的意思取决于语境：a reference to sth 常是“提及”；for reference 是“供查阅”；job reference 是“求职推荐信”。
records.examples: reference: Some tweets used the reference to directly attack the Clinton campaign. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2015/apr/13/hillary-clinton-logo-twin-towers-9-11]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · reference (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: A source or item of material consulted or recommended for further study; here, the additional works listed by the professor.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) A mention of a person or thing in speech or writing.
2) The act of consulting material to find information.
3) A number, word or symbol used to locate information.
4) The act of consulting someone for advice.
5) A job recommendation, or the person who provides one.
6) A citation showing where information in a book comes from.
7) reference (verb, formal): to cite a source or provide a text with references.

records.definition: 为日后查考而写下的备忘记录。本文 this memorandum 指教授列出的补充参考书目或清单。
records.otherSenses:
1) 组织内部使用的正式备忘录。
2) 法律用语：协议内容的初步书面记录。
3) 关于某个专题的书面建议或报告。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
an internal memorandum 内部备忘录
memorandum of understanding 谅解备忘录
a memorandum on sth 关于某事的书面报告
this memorandum 本文指教授列出的参考资料清单

Contrast:
memorandum：较正式的书面备忘或记录
memo：memorandum 的常用简称，语气较日常
note：简短记录或便条，通常更不正式

Usage Note:
memorandum 是可数名词，复数 memoranda 或 memorandums；简称 memo，复数 memos。本文 this memorandum 回指教授列出的补充参考书目。
records.examples: memorandum: The Scottish and UK governments will draw up and agree a memorandum of understanding to ensure that devolution is not detrimental to UK-wide critical national infrastructure in relation to matters such as defence and security, oil and gas and energy. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2014/nov/27/scottish-devolution-smith-commission-key-points]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · memorandum (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: A written note or record kept for future reference; here, the professor's list of additional references or reading.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) A formal note sent within an organization.
2) In law, a preliminary written record of an agreement.
3) A written proposal or report on a particular subject.

records.definition: 在某个问题或观点上存在差异、意见不一致。本文指两本书在若干问题上的说法不同。
records.otherSenses:
1) differ from/in：与某人或事物不同，或在某一方面不同。
2) differ with somebody：与某人意见不同。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
differ on several points 在若干点上意见不同
differ on how to proceed 对如何推进看法不同
agree to differ 同意保留分歧、不再争论

Contrast:
differ on：在某个议题上的说法或观点不同
disagree about：对某议题有分歧，强调意见不一致
diverge over：在某议题上逐渐形成不同看法，较正式

Usage Note:
本文主语是 two different books，differed on several points 指书中叙述或立场在若干点上不同。on 后接争议的议题；不能把 differ on sb 用来表示“不同意某人”。
records.examples: differ on: Realists differ on how much power is enough. [https://app.ludwig.guru/s/differ+on]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · differ (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: To have different opinions or accounts concerning a particular issue; here, for two books to give different views on several points.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) differ from/in: to be different from someone or something, or different in a particular respect.
2) differ with someone: to disagree with that person.

records.definition: 在某一领域被公认为可靠的权威资料或著作。本文 the other authorities 指作者继续查阅的其他权威来源。
records.otherSenses:
1) 发号施令或行使管辖的权力。
2) 做某事的正式职权或许可。
3) the authorities：有决策权的当局或主管机构。
4) 因知识或职位受到尊重而具有的威信。
5) 权威人士；专家。本文的 authorities 多指权威资料或著作，其他语境也可以指人。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a leading authority on history 历史领域的权威
consult an authority 查阅权威资料
local authorities 地方当局
have the authority to do sth 有权做某事

Contrast:
authority：某领域公认的权威人物或权威来源
expert：具备专门知识的人，不一定已获广泛认可
authoritative source：被认为可信且有分量的资料来源

Usage Note:
Turning to the other authorities 中 authorities 是复数，指其他可依凭的权威书籍或作者，不是政府部门。authority on + 领域 表示“某领域的权威”。
records.examples: authority: As president, Putin moved quickly to consolidate his authority over the economy and politics. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2014/jun/09/-sp-profiles-post-soviet-states]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · authority (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: A person or source whose knowledge or judgement is accepted as reliable; here, other authoritative writers or works consulted by the author.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) The power to give orders or exercise control.
2) The official right or permission to act.
3) the authorities: officials or bodies with decision-making power.
4) Influence that comes from respected knowledge or position.
5) a person with expert knowledge who is accepted as a reliable source

records.definition: 对某个问题持不同意见或有不同说法。本文指不同权威资料对同一批事实以及其他事实并不一致。
records.otherSenses: 1) disagree with somebody：（食物、气候等）使某人身体不适；不是“意见不同”的意思。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
disagree on the facts 对事实的说法不同
disagree on a policy 对政策有分歧
disagree with sb about sth 与某人就某事意见不同
agree to disagree 同意保留分歧

Contrast:
disagree on：对某议题持不同意见
differ on：在某议题上的说法或观点不同，语气较中性
be at odds over：因某议题而意见相左，常暗示较明显的冲突

Usage Note:
本文 they 指前面的 authorities；disagreed on the same facts 是“对同一批事实的解释或记载不一致”，不表示事实本身发生改变。
records.examples: disagree on: Disagreement between us is nothing new – we disagree on a lot of things and that’s OK. [https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2016/feb/20/a-letter-to-my-mother-who-wont-accept-we-dont-want-children]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · disagree (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: To hold different opinions or give different accounts concerning an issue; here, for authorities to conflict over the same facts and additional facts.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) disagree with somebody: of food or a climate, make a person feel ill or uncomfortable

records.definition: 向某人恳求帮助；原句中的 appealed to 是省略式，表示“有人向这位图书管理员求助”。
records.otherSenses:
1) appeal to somebody：对某人有吸引力；引起兴趣。
2) appeal：（法律等）上诉；申诉；要求复议。
3) appeal（名词）：呼吁、请求；上诉；吸引力。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
appeal to sb for help 向某人求助
appeal to sb to do sth 呼吁某人做某事
appeal to sb's interests 吸引某人的兴趣
appeal against a decision 对决定提出上诉
appeal to reason/common sense 诉诸理性／常识

Contrast:
appeal to sb for help：向某人恳切求助
ask sb for help：普通、中性的求助表达
request assistance from sb：正式地请求某人协助

Usage Note:
The librarian, appealed to, ... 中 appealed to 是补充性的过去分词短语，意为“被求助”。被动结构保留介词 to；主动句可说 appeal to the librarian for help。
records.examples: appeal to sb for help: The widow of friendly fire victim Matty Hull today appealed to the US president for help in finding out the truth about her husband's death. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2007/mar/15/military.world]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · appeal (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: To make an earnest request to someone for help; in the original sentence, appealed to means that the librarian was asked for assistance.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) appeal to somebody: attract or interest a person
2) appeal: ask a higher court or other authority to review and change a decision
3) appeal: a request for help, a legal request for review, or an attractive quality

records.definition: 短暂拜访某人；原句表示作者随后去拜访 Jones 教授。
records.otherSenses:
1) 正式请求或要求某人做某事。
2) 正式请某人发言。
3) call on/upon sth：运用、调动某种品质、技能或资源。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
call on/upon sb 拜访某人
call on sb to do sth 正式要求某人做某事
call on a customer 拜访客户

Contrast:
call on sb：拜访某人，此义较正式
visit sb：普通地拜访某人，停留时间可长可短
pay a visit to sb：较正式地说去拜访某人

Usage Note:
call on sb 在本文是“拜访某人”；call on sb to do sth 则表示“要求某人做某事”。介词 on 后接拜访对象，是否接 to do 会改变短语的意思。
records.examples: call on: However, I remember an embarrassing moment in New York, in 1989, when I called on Chinua Achebe at an NYU-run apartment block in which he was staying. [https://www.theguardian.com/books/2008/jul/22/keywords.novelists.lethem.thirlwell.farah.meek]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · call on / call (visit sense checked in the Oxford call verb entry) (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: To make a short visit to someone; in the source sentence, the writer then went to visit Professor Jones.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) call on/upon someone to do something: to formally ask or demand that they act.
2) call on/upon someone: to formally invite them to speak.
3) call on/upon something: use a quality, skill or resource when it is needed

records.definition: 勤奋；勤勉。教授称赞的是作者查阅资料时表现出的用功和努力。
records.otherSenses:
1) 工业；尤其指工厂制造业。
2) 某一行业及其从业人员。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
hard work and industry 勤奋努力
show great industry 表现得十分勤奋
an industrious student 勤奋的学生

Contrast:
industry：持续、勤勉地做事，此义较正式
diligence：认真细致并坚持不懈
hard work：普通说法，强调付出的努力

Usage Note:
本文 industry 是不可数名词，表示勤奋；表示某一行业时可数，如 the film industry。形容词 industrious 指“勤奋的”，industrial 指“工业的”。
records.examples: industry: His application, his industry, and his consistent diligence – astonished me. [https://www.theguardian.com/books/2016/aug/22/books-to-give-you-hope-prick-up-your-ears-by-john-lahr-joe-orton]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · industry (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Steady hard work and diligence; the professor is praising the effort the writer put into researching the subject.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) The production of goods, especially in factories.
2) A particular field of business and the people in it.

records.definition: 好奇、求知欲强的；作者研究史料是因为真想弄明白问题，而非为了显得听话。
records.otherSenses: 1) 奇怪的；不同寻常的。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
be curious about sth 对……好奇
be curious to know 想知道
a curious child 好奇的孩子
out of curiosity 出于好奇

Contrast:
curious：想了解未知事物，强调求知欲
inquisitive：爱提问、探究；有时也暗示爱打听
eager to learn：渴望学习，强调学习意愿

Usage Note:
be curious about + 名词／疑问词从句；be curious to do sth 表示“很想知道而去做”。本文 a curious boy 与 a good boy 对照，意思是他的努力来自求知欲，不是为了表现乖巧。
records.examples: curious: Today's young people are inquisitive, curious and want their information to be easily digestible, as well as fun. [https://www.theguardian.com/higher-education-network/blog/2014/feb/17/how-to-recruit-attract-university-students]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · curious (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Eager to learn and understand; the writer researched history out of curiosity, not to seem obedient.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) Strange or unusual.

records.definition: 难以解释、尚未得到答案的问题；这里指史料之间的矛盾反而使疑问更深。
records.otherSenses:
1) 因了解不多而显得神秘的人或事物。
2) 神秘感；难以解释而引人入胜的特质。
3) 结尾才揭晓谜底的悬疑作品。
4) 不能用科学解释或证明的宗教奥义。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
solve a mystery 解开谜团
remain a mystery 仍是谜
deepen the mystery 加深谜团
be a mystery to sb 对某人是个谜

Contrast:
mystery：尚未得到解释的事，可能引起探究
enigma：难以理解的人或事，较书面
puzzle：令人费解、需要想出答案的问题

Usage Note:
指一个未解问题时可数：a mystery；表示神秘感时用作不可数名词：an air of mystery。
本文不是指某个被故意隐瞒的秘密，而是尚待研究的历史问题。
mystery 的复数是 mysteries。
records.examples: mystery: To my genuine astonishment, I too find life is fine with only the essentials and what's in those boxes has become a mystery to me, although not an intriguing one. [https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2015/may/01/do-something-decluttering]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · mystery (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: A question or situation that is difficult to explain and has not yet been answered; here, conflicting historical sources deepen the uncertainty.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) A person or thing that seems strange because little is known about them.
2) The quality of being difficult to explain, especially in an intriguing way.
3) A story, film or play whose crime or puzzle is explained at the end.
4) A religious belief that cannot be scientifically explained or proved.

records.definition: 把问题解释清楚或解决；原句指书籍澄清了那个历史问题。
records.otherSenses:
1) 指天气：放晴。
2) 指疾病或感染：消失、痊愈。
3) 收拾、整理某个地方。
4) clear-up（英式名词）：打扫、清理。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
clear up a mystery/problem 解开谜团／解决问题（本文）
clear up confusion/a misunderstanding 消除困惑／误会
the weather clears up 天气放晴
a rash clears up 皮疹消退
clear up a mess 收拾乱摊子

Contrast:
clear up：把问题或误会解释清楚
resolve：把问题或争议最终解决
solve：找出问题、谜题的答案

Usage Note:
clear up 是可分短语动词：clear the problem up / clear it up。本文 clearing up the historical question 表示“把历史问题解释清楚”。
records.examples: clear up: Take antibiotics to clear up your infection. [https://www.wikihow.com/Recognize-Staph-Infection-Symptoms]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · clear up (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: To solve or explain a problem or mystery so that it becomes understood; in the source sentence, a book clarified the historical question.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Of weather: to become fine or bright.
2) Of an illness or infection: to disappear.
3) To tidy a place by putting things away.
4) clear-up (noun, British English): an act of tidying and removing rubbish.

records.definition: 深深吸引、使着迷；本文 I was fascinated 表示作者被历史研究深深吸引。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
be fascinated by/with sth 对……着迷
be fascinated to learn/hear ... 得知／听到……而极感兴趣
fascination with sth 对……的着迷

Contrast:
fascinate：深深吸引，使人很感兴趣
captivate：迷住、牢牢吸引人的注意，感情色彩更强
intrigue：引起好奇与兴趣，常带未解之谜的意味

Usage Note:
fascinate sb 是及物动词；人感到着迷可说 be fascinated by/with sth，令人着迷的事物可用 fascinating 修饰。本文 I was fascinated 说的是作者的感受。
records.examples: fascinate: When it comes to Henry VIII the drama never seems to end, which is why his colourful life continues to fascinate us. [https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/wolf-hall-episode-5-tv-review-damian-lewis-is-so-good-as-the-capricious-king-that-you-want-to-slap-him-10054169.html]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · fascinate (fascinated interpreted from the verb entry in context) (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: To attract and interest someone very strongly; in “I was fascinated,” the author became absorbed in his historical research.

records.definition: 本质性的；根本的。essential differences 指观点和事实方面并非细枝末节的重大差异。
records.otherSenses:
1) essentials（复数名词）：必需品。
2) essentials（复数名词）：某学科的要点或基础知识。
3) 必不可少的；必要的。注意：原文 essential differences 侧重“根本性的差异”，这里是其常见的“必要”义。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
an essential difference 根本差异
the essential nature of sth 某事物的本质
be essential to/for sth 对……必不可少
the bare essentials 最基本的必需品

Contrast:
essential：本文指触及本质的、根本性的
fundamental：涉及基础或根本层面
substantive：有实际内容或重大影响，不是表面上的

Usage Note:
essential differences 应按“根本／实质性差异”理解，不能译成“必要的差异”。
essential to/for 后接名词或 doing；It is essential to do sth 中 to 引出不定式。
essentially 常意为“本质上／基本上”，不是“一定要”。
records.examples: essential: "Intolerance of corruption is essential to the survival of our representative democracy and way of life," he said. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2015/feb/09/coal-approvals-must-be-overhauled-to-stop-corruption-says-former-nsw-watchdog]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · essential (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Fundamental and central rather than minor; essential differences are major differences in viewpoints and facts.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) essentials (plural noun): things that are necessary.
2) essentials (plural noun): the main facts or basic knowledge of a subject.
3) absolutely needed; too important to do without

records.definition: 在没有确证时推想、怀疑某事可能属实；作者由研究产生了对制宪者真实意图的怀疑。
records.otherSenses:
1) 怀疑某人做错事或违法。
2) 怀疑某事物的诚实性或可靠性。
3) suspect（名词）：嫌疑人。
4) suspect（形容词）：可疑的；不可靠的。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
suspect that ... 认为……很可能
suspect sb of doing sth 怀疑某人做了某事
suspect foul play 怀疑有人作恶
I suspect so/not. 我想是／不是。

Contrast:
suspect：认为某事可能属实，但证据尚不足以确认
surmise：根据有限线索作出推测，较正式
conjecture：在缺乏足够证据时猜测，语气更试探

Usage Note:
suspect 作动词时重音在后 /səˈspekt/，作名词“嫌疑人”时重音在前 /ˈsʌspekt/。suspect that ... 表认为某事可能属实；suspect sb of sth 表怀疑某人做了某事。
records.examples: suspect: People already suspect this is a recovery for the rich and ongoing recession for the rest. [https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2013/sep/24/ed-miliband-labour-conference-speech-verdict]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · suspect (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: To think that something is probably true without having definite proof; the writer's research led him to doubt the constitution-makers' real intentions.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) To believe someone may have done something wrong or illegal.
2) To distrust something's honesty or reliability.
3) suspect (noun): a person thought to have committed a crime.
4) suspect (adjective): possibly false, dangerous or unreliable.

records.definition: 被视为至高、不可质疑而受到崇敬的；这里的 sacred Constitution 带有对传统神圣化态度的暗示。
records.otherSenses:
1) 与神或宗教有关；神圣的。
2) 特别珍贵的；不容侵犯或随意改变的，可用于个人隐私、回忆等非宗教事物。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a sacred text/site 宗教经典／圣地
a sacred duty 神圣职责
be sacred to sb 对某人而言神圣不可侵犯

Contrast:
sacred：因宗教、文化或情感而受到高度尊崇
sacrosanct：被视为不可质疑或侵犯，尤用于非宗教语境
revered：备受崇敬，强调人们持有的态度

Usage Note:
本文 sacred 带修辞意味：宪法受到近乎神圣的尊崇。不要机械译为“宗教性的宪法”。
sacred 是两音节 /ˈseɪkrɪd/，结尾不是 /kt/。
records.examples: sacred: It is a sacred moment, and you feel blessed merely to have witnessed it. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2015/feb/08/poor-glasgow-safe-seat-cranhill-labour-snp-election-voters]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · sacred (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Regarded with such deep reverence that it should not be questioned or challenged; sacred Constitution hints at a tradition of treating the document as untouchable.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Connected with God, a god or religion; holy.
2) treated as especially precious or deserving protection, often for personal reasons

records.definition: 民主的；由人民选出的代表治理、体现人民政治权利的。
records.otherSenses:
1) 让组织成员平等参与管理或决策。
2) 强调社会成员平等，而非按财富或阶级区分。
3) Democratic（首字母大写）：美国民主党的。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
democratic government 民主政府
democratic process 民主程序
democratic election 民主选举

Usage Note:
democratic government 指民主政体或民主政府；小写 democratic 是普通形容词。大写 Democratic 可指美国民主党，不能把两者混同。
records.examples: democratic: In the post-war period the Fabian Society was at the heart of Labour and social democratic thinking. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2001/aug/13/thinktanks.uk]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · democratic (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Based on government by elected representatives and on the political rights of the people.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) Giving members equal rights to participate in an organization's decisions.
2) Based on social equality rather than wealth or class.
3) Democratic (capitalized): relating to the US Democratic Party.

records.definition: 拿破仑·波拿巴；原句说作者童年时会在想象游戏中把自己当作拿破仑。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
Napoleon Bonaparte 拿破仑·波拿巴
the Napoleonic Wars 拿破仑战争
Napoleonic France 拿破仑时期的法国
pretend/play that one is Napoleon 假扮拿破仑

Usage Note:
Napoleon 是人名，首字母大写。原文说儿童游戏中“I was Napoleon”，相当于“我扮演拿破仑”；形容词 Napoleonic 指拿破仑本人或其时代。
records.examples: Napoleon: The Duke was given a state funeral after defeating Napoleon at Waterloo in 1815. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/w3cswsjm]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: the Napoleonic Wars（Oxford Learner’s 无 Napoleon 独立人物词条，链接包含人物说明的文化条目）
records.definitionEn: Napoleon Bonaparte, the French military leader and emperor; as a child, the writer imagined himself playing Napoleon.

records.definition: 使用陷阱捕捉动物的人；本文是作者童年想象扮演的角色。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
fur trapper 毛皮猎人
a trapper's cabin 捕兽人的小屋

trapper：使用陷阱捕捉动物的人
hunter：从事猎捕的人，方法不限于陷阱
fur trapper：专为获取毛皮设陷阱捕猎者

Usage Note:
trapper 是可数名词，复数 trappers。动词 trap 加 -ed、-ing 或 -er 时双写 p：trapped、trapping、trapper；不表示所有 hunter 都使用陷阱。
records.examples: trapper: The last major atrocity was triggered by a fight about an indigenous woman that lead to a white dingo trapper being murdered. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2010/oct/03/alice-spring-murder-racism]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: trapper（该词通常只有这一核心义）
records.definitionEn: A person who catches animals using traps; here, one of the roles the writer imagined playing as a child.

records.definition: 制作、形成的过程；the making of the American Constitution 指美国宪法的制定过程。
records.otherSenses:
1) be the making of somebody：使某人成长或获得成功。
2) have the makings of something：具备成为某事物的素质。
3) in the making：正在形成或制作中。
4) of your own making：由自己造成的。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
the making of a film 电影制作过程
the making of a constitution 宪法制定过程
in the making 在形成中

Contrast:
the making of：形成或制作的过程
creation：从无到有的创造或成果
formation：事物逐渐形成的过程

Usage Note:
这里 making 有 the 限定，并用 of 引出对象，是表示过程的名词化形式；不是进行时。
the making of a film 是拍摄／制作过程；be the making of sb 则指使某人成功的重要因素。
records.examples: making:Controversy was the making of the prize. [https://www.newyorker.com/?p=1969901]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · making (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: The process of creating or forming something; the making of the American Constitution means the process by which the Constitution was produced.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) be the making of someone: to help them become better or more successful.
2) have the makings of something: to have the qualities needed to become it.
3) in the making: in the process of being created or formed.
4) of your own making: caused by your own actions.

records.definition: 具有鲜明特点的一段历史时期；本文 eras 泛指不同时代。
records.otherSenses: 1) 地质学：宙之下的一个年代划分，即“代”。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a new era 新时代
the modern era 现代
an era of change 变革时代
the Common Era 公元（CE）

era：以事件或特征界定的一段历史时期
epoch：影响重大的历史时期，较正式
age：具有鲜明特征的时代，也可指年龄

era 是可数名词，复数为 eras。本文 other events, men, and eras 是并列宾语，后面的 waiting for students 是现在分词短语，修饰三者。
records.examples: era: The era when Nigeria's rulers could take the people for granted is no more. [https://www.theguardian.com/global/commentisfree/2015/mar/31/nigeria-election-muhammadu-buhari-revolution-voted-change]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · era (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: A historical period marked by distinctive events or characteristics; here, eras means different historical periods.
records.otherSensesEn: 1) In geology, a major division of time below an eon.

records.definition: 彼此说法不一致的；disagreeing authorities 指对历史事实或解释持不同意见的权威资料或学者。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
disagree with sb 不同意某人
disagree about/on/over sth 对某事意见不一
strongly/fundamentally disagree 强烈／根本不同意
disagreeing accounts 相互矛盾的说法
agree to disagree 同意保留分歧

Contrast:
disagreeing：彼此观点或说法不一致的
conflicting：相互矛盾的，冲突通常更明显
divergent：逐渐分开的、不同的，较正式

Usage Note:
本文 disagreeing authorities 指“观点相互冲突的权威作者”。谈论意见时通常说 disagree with somebody、disagree about/on something。
records.examples: disagreeing: The talks are progressing slowly, with countries still disagreeing over issues such as finance from developed to poor countries, helping them cut emissions and adapt to climate change, and the wording of the final text. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2012/dec/06/doha-conference-black-carbon-methane]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · disagree (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Holding different opinions or giving conflicting accounts; disagreeing authorities are experts or sources that do not agree about historical facts or their interpretation.

records.definition: 起决定作用的；能最终证实结论的。clinching evidence 指足以定论的确凿证据。
records.otherSenses:
1) clinch：最终敲定；解决；赢得。
2) clinch：紧紧抱住；（拳击中）抱住对手。
3) clinch（名词）：（拳击）扭抱；紧紧拥抱。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
clinching evidence 决定性证据
clinch a deal 敲定交易
clinch a victory/title 锁定胜利／冠军

Contrast:
clinching：足以使问题或争论最终定论
conclusive：证据足以支持最终结论，较正式
decisive：在结果上起决定作用，不限于证据

Usage Note:
clinching 在本文修饰 evidence，表示足以定论。词典中的 clinch 读 /klɪntʃ/，加 -ing 后读 /ˈklɪntʃɪŋ/。
clinch 常见于新闻和非正式表达，不能把它笼统标成正式词；较正式论证可用 conclusive evidence。
不要与 cinch“轻而易举的事／束紧”混淆。
records.examples: cliching: It is odd that this was regarded as a clinching argument, as there are more than enough jets in Afghanistan. [https://www.economist.com/britain/2010/11/11/the-seat-of-their-pants]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary: clinch (verb)（clinching 作为派生形式列在父词条）
records.definitionEn: Decisive and sufficient to settle a question; clinching evidence is proof strong enough to establish a conclusion finally.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) clinch: finally settle an argument, confirm an agreement or secure a victory
2) clinch: hold somebody tightly, especially in boxing or an embrace
3) clinch: a tight hold in boxing or a close embrace

records.definition: 虚荣心；对自己的外表、能力或成就过度自负。
records.otherSenses:
1) 文学用法：与重大问题相比的渺小、无足轻重。
2) vanities（复数）：表现虚荣的行为或态度。
3) 北美英语：带抽屉和镜子的梳妆台。
4) （文学）虚妄；徒劳；人的追求缺乏长久意义。
5) （尤北美英语）带洗脸盆的浴室柜；盥洗台。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
personal vanity 个人虚荣
appeal to sb's vanity 满足某人的虚荣
vanity about sth 对……的虚荣

Contrast:
vanity：过分在意自己的外表、才能或成就
conceit：过高评价自己的能力或重要性
self-importance：自以为重要，突出自我中心

Usage Note:
本文 vanity 是不可数抽象名词，指虚荣心。then 限定的是作者当时的主要动机，不等于说他从不虚荣。
vanities 是表现虚荣的行为；vanity 在北美英语还可指梳妆台。
records.examples: vanity: He was no stranger to vanity, and would make good use of his appearance. https://www.economist.com/baobab/2013/12/05/the-long-walk-is-over[]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · vanity (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Excessive pride in one’s appearance, abilities or achievements; here, the desire to impress others was not the author’s chief motive.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) In literary use, the unimportance of something compared with matters such as death.
2) vanities (plural): acts or attitudes showing excessive pride.
3) In North American English, a dressing table with drawers and a mirror.
4) futility or the failure of human efforts to achieve lasting value
5) a bathroom cabinet or unit with a washbasin built into its top

records.definition: 占支配地位的；主导的。ruling passion 指最强烈、最能支配一个人的欲望或激情。
records.otherSenses:
1) ruling（形容词）：执政或统治的。
2) ruling（名词）：正式裁决，尤其是法官作出的裁定。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a ruling passion 主导性的热情
a passion for history 对历史的热爱
be driven by curiosity 受好奇心驱动

Contrast:
ruling：起主导或支配作用
dominant：在多个力量或因素中占优势
prevailing：在某时或某地最普遍、最有影响力

Usage Note:
本文 ruling 在名词 passion 前作定语，指“支配性的、主导的”；不是 was ruling 的进行时结构。
不要与名词 ruling（正式裁决）混淆。
records.examples: ruling: The opposition said it was a device to help the ruling party. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/mar/10/foreign-troops-retake-nigerian-towns-from-boko-haram]
records.dictionaryLabel: Oxford Advanced Learner's English-Chinese Dictionary (10th Edition) · ruling (context sense from rule; ruling noun and adjective entries also checked) (user-provided Oxford excerpt)
records.definitionEn: Having the strongest influence or control; a ruling passion is the most powerful desire or emotion governing a person.
records.otherSensesEn:
1) ruling (adjective): governing or having control over a group or country.
2) ruling (noun): an official decision, especially by a judge.

records.definition: 正在增强、变得活跃的；a quickening sense 指逐渐强烈起来的意识。
records.otherSenses:
1) 指速度或节奏：加快。
2) quickening（医学名词）：孕妇首次感觉到胎动；不是本文“逐渐增强的意识”的形容词用法。
records.supplementation:
Pattern & Collocation:
a quickening sense of purpose 逐渐增强的目标感
